source.primary_witnesses: Aramaic DSS fragments (4Q201-4Q207; late 3rd c. BCE through 1st c. BCE) where preserved; Greek Akhmim Panopolitanus (6th c. CE) where Aramaic absent; Ge'ez (medieval; the only complete witness) as fallback
source.transliteration_convention: Scholarly conventions: Aramaic Imperial-Aramaic transliteration per Milik 1976 (ḥ ṣ ʿ ḫ); Greek SBL convention (η→ē, ω→ō, θ→th, etc., matching Matthew precedent); Ge'ez SBL Ge'ez convention (ḫ ḫ̣ ʾ ʿ ä for ä-vowel)
source.verificationStatus: best-effort reconstruction; verification pending against Milik 1976 DJD apparatus + Nickelsburg 2001 Hermeneia + original codicology
source.fetchedFrom: Milik 1976 The Books of Enoch + Black 1985 Greek text + Charles 1912 Ge'ez PD + Knibb 1978 Ge'ez critical edition + Nickelsburg 2001 Hermeneia commentary
source.citation: Milik 1976 The Books of Enoch (Oxford); Black 1985 The Book of Enoch or 1 Enoch (SVTP 7, Leiden); Nickelsburg 2001 1 Enoch 1 Hermeneia; Charles 1912 The Book of Enoch (Oxford, PD); Knibb 1978 The Ethiopic Book of Enoch (Oxford); Tigchelaar-García Martínez 2000 DJD XXXVI; VanderKam 1984 Enoch and the Growth of an Apocalyptic Tradition; Reed 2005 Fallen Angels; Olyan 1993 A Thousand Thousands Served Him.
source.paleography_note: CHAPTER 20 — THE SEVEN ARCHANGELS — Aramaic 4Q204 1 vii preserves partial; **the Aramaic list is shorter (only 4 archangels preserved/extant); Greek expands to 7**; Ge'ez has 7 with slight name variation (Sariel vs Saraqael). **MAJOR LENS-RISK + TEXT-CRITICAL SITE — preserve textual dispute in apparatus.**

verses.text_greek: Καὶ οὗτοι ὀνόματα τῶν ἁγίων ἀγγέλων τῶν ἐγρηγορούντων.
verses.translit: Kai houtoi onomata tōn hagiōn angelōn tōn egrēgorountōn.
verses.text_aramaic: ואלן שמהת מלאכיא קדישיא די עירין
verses.text_geez: ወዝንቱ፡ አስማተ፡ መላእክት፡ ቅዱሳን፡ እለ፡ ይትገሃዱ፡
verses.witness_primary: 4Q204 1 vii 14 (Milik 1976 pp. 232-233) — Aramaic incipit of archangel-list preserved
verses.notes: Heading: 'These are the names of the holy angels who watch.' The participle ἐγρηγορούντων / עירין designates these as the loyal/wakeful Watchers (in contrast to the fallen Watchers of ch 6). The headed-list form is characteristic of Second Temple angelological literature.

verses.text_greek: Οὐριήλ, ὁ εἷς τῶν ἁγίων ἀγγέλων, ὁ ἐπὶ τοῦ κόσμου καὶ τοῦ ταρτάρου.
verses.translit: Ouriēl, ho heis tōn hagiōn angelōn, ho epi tou kosmou kai tou tartarou.
verses.text_aramaic: אוריאל חד מן מלאכיא קדישיא די על תבל ועל תהומא
verses.text_geez: ዑርኤል፡ አሐዱ፡ እመላእክት፡ ቅዱሳን፡ ዘላዕለ፡ ዓለም፡ ወታርታሮስ፡
verses.witness_primary: 4Q204 1 vii 15 (Milik 1976 pp. 232-234) — Aramaic of Uriel preserved
verses.notes: **URIEL** ('My light is God / God is my light') — over the world and Tartarus. The Greek τάρταρος is here borrowed for cosmic-underworld jurisdiction. Cross-corpus: 2 Pet 2:4 (the verb ταρταρόω 'cast into Tartarus' for fallen angels — Petrine adoption of 1 Enoch's vocabulary). Uriel reappears as guide-figure in 1 En 17-19, 21:5, 33:3-4, 72-82; in 2 Esd 4-5; in Hekhalot literature.

verses.text_greek: Ῥαφαήλ, ὁ εἷς τῶν ἁγίων ἀγγέλων, ὁ ἐπὶ τῶν πνευμάτων τῶν ἀνθρώπων.
verses.translit: Raphaēl, ho heis tōn hagiōn angelōn, ho epi tōn pneumatōn tōn anthrōpōn.
verses.text_aramaic: רפאל חד מן מלאכיא קדישיא די על רוחי בני אנשא
verses.text_geez: ሩፋኤል፡ አሐዱ፡ እመላእክት፡ ቅዱሳን፡ ዘላዕለ፡ መናፍስተ፡ ሰብእ፡
verses.witness_primary: 4Q204 1 vii 16 (Milik 1976 pp. 232-234) — Aramaic of Raphael preserved
verses.notes: **RAPHAEL** ('God has healed') — over the spirits of human beings. Cross-corpus: Tobit 3:17, 12:15 (Raphael as one of 'the seven holy angels'); 1 En 10:4 (Raphael binds Azazel). The healing-physician-angel motif feeds rabbinic + Christian angelology.

verses.text_greek: Ῥαγουήλ, ὁ εἷς τῶν ἁγίων ἀγγέλων, ὁ ἐπὶ τοῦ κόσμου τῶν φωστήρων.
verses.translit: Raguēl, ho heis tōn hagiōn angelōn, ho epi tou kosmou tōn phōstērōn.
verses.text_aramaic: רעואל חד מן מלאכיא קדישיא די על נהוריא
verses.text_geez: ራጉኤል፡ አሐዱ፡ እመላእክት፡ ቅዱሳን፡ ዘላዕለ፡ ዓለመ፡ ብርሃናት፡
verses.witness_primary: 4Q204 1 vii 17 (Milik 1976 pp. 232-234) — Aramaic of Raguel preserved
verses.notes: **RAGUEL / RA'UEL** ('friend of God') — over the world of the luminaries. The luminary-jurisdiction matches the astronomical concern of the book. Raguel is a guide-figure later in 1 En 23:4.

verses.text_greek: Μιχαήλ, ὁ εἷς τῶν ἁγίων ἀγγέλων, ὁ ἐπὶ τῶν τοῦ λαοῦ ἀγαθῶν τεταγμένος καὶ ἐπὶ τοῦ χάους.
verses.translit: Michaēl, ho heis tōn hagiōn angelōn, ho epi tōn tou laou agathōn tetagmenos kai epi tou chaous.
verses.text_aramaic: מיכאל חד מן מלאכיא קדישיא די על טבת עמא ועל פהיא
verses.text_geez: ሚካኤል፡ አሐዱ፡ እመላእክት፡ ቅዱሳን፡ ዘላዕለ፡ ሠናያተ፡ ሕዝብ፡ ሥሩዕ፡ ወላዕለ፡ ሕዝብ፡
verses.witness_primary: 4Q204 1 vii 18 (Milik 1976 pp. 232-234) — Aramaic of Michael preserved; the 4-archangel-list ends here in the Aramaic
verses.notes: **MICHAEL** ('Who is like God') — set over the best part of humanity and over chaos. **TEXT-CRITICAL NOTE: This is where the surviving Aramaic 4Q204 list ENDS — only 4 archangels (Uriel, Raphael, Raguel, Michael) are preserved in the Aramaic.** The Greek + Ge'ez continue with three more (Saraqael, Gabriel, Remiel), yielding the seven-archangel canonical list. Whether the Aramaic original had 7 names that are now lost, or had only 4 with the expansion being a Greek-period editorial development, is **textually disputed** (cf. Milik 1976 pp. 174-176; Nickelsburg 2001 pp. 294-296; Tigchelaar 1999). Cross-corpus: Dan 10:13, 21; 12:1 (Michael as 'great prince'); Jude 9 (Michael disputing with the devil over Moses' body); Rev 12:7 (Michael and his angels fight the dragon).

verses.text_greek: Σαρακαήλ, ὁ εἷς τῶν ἁγίων ἀγγέλων, ὁ ἐπὶ τῶν πνευμάτων τῶν ἁμαρτωλῶν.
verses.translit: Sarakaēl, ho heis tōn hagiōn angelōn, ho epi tōn pneumatōn tōn hamartōlōn.
verses.text_geez: ሰራቅኤል፡ አሐዱ፡ እመላእክት፡ ቅዱሳን፡ ዘላዕለ፡ መናፍስት፡ እለ፡ ይሴስሉ፡ ሰብአ፡ ለኀጢአት፡
verses.notes: **SARAQAEL / SARIEL** — over the spirits that lead humans to sin. The Ge'ez tradition often has SARIEL ('command of God') instead of SARAQAEL — the two are likely identical with name-variants. cf. 1 En 9:1 (Sariel listed among the four chief angels in some manuscripts); 4QEnª (Sariel attested at Qumran in connection with Michael, Gabriel, Raphael). **TEXT-CRITICAL — name variation: Greek Sarakaēl / Ge'ez Saraqael / 4Q Sariel.** Modern angelology often distinguishes 'Sariel' as a separate archangel, but in Second Temple usage they are likely conflated.

verses.text_greek: Γαβριήλ, ὁ εἷς τῶν ἁγίων ἀγγέλων, ὁ ἐπὶ τοῦ παραδείσου καὶ τῶν δρακόντων καὶ Χερουβίν.
verses.translit: Gabriēl, ho heis tōn hagiōn angelōn, ho epi tou paradeisou kai tōn drakontōn kai Cheroubin.
verses.text_geez: ገብርኤል፡ አሐዱ፡ እመላእክት፡ ቅዱሳን፡ ዘላዕለ፡ ገነት፡ ወዘላዕለ፡ አርዌ፡ ምድር፡ ወኪሩቤል፡
verses.notes: **GABRIEL** ('God is my strength') — over paradise, the serpents, and the cherubim. Cross-corpus: Dan 8:16, 9:21 (Gabriel as revealer-angel); Lk 1:19, 26 (Gabriel announces John and Jesus); Qur'an 2:97-98 (Jibrīl as revealer of the Qur'an). The 'over the dragons' jurisdiction (drakontōn) connects to Gen 3 (serpent) and Rev 12 (the great dragon Michael fights — although there it's Michael, not Gabriel).

verses.text_greek: Ῥεμιήλ, ὃν ἔταξεν ὁ θεὸς ἐπὶ τῶν ἀνισταμένων.
verses.translit: Remiēl, hon etaxen ho theos epi tōn anistamenōn.
verses.text_geez: ረሚኤል፡ ዘሤሞ፡ እግዚአብሔር፡ ዲበ፡ እለ፡ ይትነሥኡ፡
verses.notes: **REMIEL / JERAHMEEL** ('God has mercy' / 'God exalts') — over those who rise (i.e., the resurrected). Cross-corpus: 2 Esd 4:36 (Jeremiel = same figure presiding over souls awaiting resurrection); 2 Bar 55:3. **The seventh-archangel-as-resurrection-guardian completes the canonical septenary list** that anchors all subsequent Jewish + Christian + Islamic angelology of the seven archangels (cf. Tob 12:15 'I am Raphael, one of the seven holy angels'; Rev 8:2 'the seven angels who stand before God'; Rev 1:4 'seven spirits before the throne'). **MAJOR CANON-ENGAGEMENT TERMINUS — the seven-archangels-list of 1 En 20 is the foundational angelological text for the post-biblical septenary tradition.**
